# Guide to Pumble Addons

6 min read

 isidora.komaromi@cake.com

Who can use this feature?
Owner, Admin, Member

Available on all plans

Pumble’s integrations seamlessly connect various software tools (e.g., Google Drive, Calendly, Polls, GitHub), making collaboration easier within your workspace. By consolidating all your essential tools, Pumble reduces unnecessary steps and simplifies workflows, creating effective teamwork.

This guide will walk you through the basics of Pumble integrations, from finding and adding addons to understanding their functionality.

| Subscription type | Maximum number of addons |
|---|---|
| Free subscription | Up to 3 addons |
| Pro plan | Up to 10 addons |
| Business and Enterprise plans | Unlimited number of addons |

Info

Only Owners and Admins can install apps. If your Workspace has Request App approval turned on, members can request an installation, and an Owner or Admin approves or declines it.

## Types of addons #

Pumble supports different types of addons. The way an app is built determines its installation, management, and interaction within your workspace.

![](https://pumble.com/help/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/Screenshot-2024-02-12-at-09.39.09-1024x352.png)

## Find and add addons #

Explore the Pumble App Directory or browse the [CAKE.com Marketplace](https://marketplace.cake.com/) to find and add addons to your workspace:

1. Click on the **three dots** next to your Workspace name
2. Hover over **Workspace settings**
3. Click on **Configure apps**
4. Click on the **Install** button next to the app you want to add
5. Click Allow on the consent screen to complete the action

You may be redirected to an external website (that app’s website) to allow the installation of the app.

Another way to install Pumble Addons is through the CAKE.com Marketplace. Here’s how you can do it:

1. Click on the **three dots** next to your Workspace name
2. Hover over **Workspace settings**
3. Click on **Configure apps**
4. Click on **Browse Marketplace**
5. Select the addon you want to install
6. Click **Install** and allow access request

Upon installation of the addon, authorization is automatically granted. Once an app is installed, other Workspace users need to go to **Workspace settings > Configure apps** and click **Authorize** to enable the app for individual use. Authorize is available only for apps already installed in the Workspace.

## Request app installation #

When the Request App Approval option is turned on, members can send installation requests for review.

To turn on app requests:

1. Click on the **three** **dots** next to your Workspace name
2. Hover over **Workspace** **settings**
3. Click on **Configure** **apps**
4. Select the **Settings** tab
5. Check the box next to **Allow members to request apps for approval**

![](https://pumble.com/help/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/turn-on-app-requests-1024x545.jpg)

Once this setting is turned on, members can request installations by following these steps:

1. Click on the **three** **dots** next to your Workspace name
2. Hover over **Workspace** **settings**
3. Click on **Configure** **apps**
4. Find the app and click Install
5. Review the permissions the app needs
6. Add a message for the approver
7. Click **Submit request**

![](https://pumble.com/help/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/request-app-installations-1024x253.jpg)

## Create your own addon from scratch #

To create your own app from scratch, follow these steps:

1. Click on the **three dots** next to the Workspace name
2. Hover over **Workspace settings**
3. Click on **Configure apps**
4. Click on **Create app**
5. Click **Create from scratch**

![](https://pumble.com/help/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image.png)

6. Provide **Display information** details in the dialog box:

- Enter **App name**
- Upload **App avatar**
- Enter a **Description** about your app

![](https://pumble.com/help/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-1-543x1024.png)

7. Configure the app **Settings**:

- Select **User scopes** and **Bot scopes** from the dropdown list
- Select an **Event** from the dropdown list
- Optional: Toggle the **Socket mode** switch to ON if you want your app to connect via Socket mode

8. Click **Create app**

9. Take note of your app credentials

10. Click **Install app**
 System displays the User token and Bot token.

11. Click **Close**

The app you created will be added to the app list.

### Create an addon from a JSON manifest #

You can create an addon by using a JSON manifest. Here’s how:

1. Click on the **three dots** next to the Workspace name
2. Click on **Workspace settings**
3. Select **Configure apps**
4. Click on **+ Create app**
5. Click on **Create from manifest**
6. Paste your JSON code
7. Click on **Next**
8. Click on **Install App**

![](https://pumble.com/help/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/Create-addon-from-JSON-manifest-1024x858.jpg)

## The addon permission scopes #

Each addon has specific permission scopes, detailing the information it can access and how that information can be used. Scopes can be related to posting messages, performing actions, and accessing information. Be aware of which information the app can access and what it can do with the information it accesses, such as posting messages, modifying content, or creating channels.

There are two types of scopes:

- User scope
- Bot scope

User scope implies that the addon can perform actions on behalf of users. If the app has a Bot scope, once installed, the addon Bot will be added to your Pumble workspace as a new user.

To view the addon scope:

1. Click on the **three dots** next to your Workspace name
2. Hover over **Workspace settings**
3. Click on **Configure apps**
4. Click on the **three dots** next to the app in question
5. Select **View scopes** from the dropdown

![](https://pumble.com/help/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/view-app-scopes.gif)

## Working with installed addons #

How you use and interact with an addon depends on how it was built. Some common features include slash commands, app shortcuts, and bot users.

### Slash commands #

Slash commands allow users to interact with the third-party addon by typing a string into the message editor.

To add a slash command:

1. Type slash icon / in the message editor
2. Select a command from the list in the pop-up
3. Type additional text for the app
4. Press Enter to complete the action

Tip

You can also access the list of all available slash commands if you hover over the Bot’s avatar, or in the channel details of your conversation with the Bot.

### Addon shortcuts #

Some addons offer shortcuts for actions in Pumble. There are two types of shortcuts:

- Global shortcuts
- Message shortcuts

To use a global shortcut:

1. Type slash icon / in the message editor
2. Select a command from the list in the pop-up
3. Press **Enter** to complete the action

It is not possible to type additional text for communication with the app.

To use a message shortcut:

1. Click on **three dots** to open a message menu
2. Select one of the listed message shortcuts

Use the slash icon to find app shortcuts or slash commands.

Certain addons have bots that send messages and post in channels. Bots are visible in the Apps section at the bottom of your Pumble sidebar.

![](https://pumble.com/help/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/Bot-users.jpeg)

## Uninstall an addon #

To uninstall a third-party addon:

1. Click on the **three dots** next to your Workspace name
2. Hover over **Workspace settings**
3. Click on **Configure apps**
4. Click on the **three dots** next to the app you want to uninstall
5. Click **Uninstall** to complete the action

![](https://pumble.com/help/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/Uninstall-an-addon.gif)

When you uninstall an addon, a toast message will appear in the bottom right corner. Also, the addon chat will be removed, and you won’t be able to see messages with the addon.

## Pumble SDK #

Pumble also offers integration with various platforms through our [Software Development Kit](https://github.com/CAKE-com/pumble-node-sdk) (SDK). Comprehensive documentation on how to build a Pumble app in javascript framework can be found [here](https://cake-com.github.io/pumble-node-sdk/).
